title: 21 Grams
events_chronological: Mathematician Paul Rivers is told that his failing heart will kill him within weeks unless a donor is found.
His estranged wife Mary presses him to agree to be inseminated with his frozen sperm before he dies.
Ex-convict Jack Jordan, newly born again, holds down a job and coaches boys' baseball while his wife Marianne dreads his fanaticism and his temper.
Cristina Peck, a recovered addict, lives a settled suburban life with her husband Michael and their two young daughters.
Jack's pickup hits Michael and both girls at a crossing; he drives off, turns back, and then flees.
Cristina is told at the hospital that her husband and both children are dead.
Michael's heart is transplanted into Paul, who wakes up alive for the first time in months.
Jack walks into a police station, confesses to the hit-and-run and is sent back to prison.
Cristina goes back to cocaine and begins methodically destroying herself.
Unable to stop thinking about whose heart is beating in his chest, Paul hires a private investigator to find the donor's widow.
Paul follows Cristina, engineers a meeting at a swimming pool, and the two begin an affair.
Paul leaves Mary and tells her he does not want the child she is trying to conceive.
Paul admits to Cristina that he is carrying Michael's heart; she throws him out, then takes him back.
Released early, Jack walks out on Marianne and on his faith and takes work at a motel far from home.
Cristina demands that Jack be killed, and Paul buys a gun and tracks him to the motel.
Paul cannot go through with it and only wounds Jack, telling him to run.
Jack follows the pair back to their motel and asks Paul to finish the job, and Paul turns the gun on himself instead.
Cristina and Jack get the dying Paul to a hospital where the transplanted heart fails; Jack goes home to his family and Cristina, pregnant, goes home alone.
syuzhet_notes: The film cuts continuously between three strands - Paul's illness and transplant, Cristina's family and bereavement, Jack's conversion and crime - with no captions, dates or dissolves to mark the jumps, so almost every told-order bullet is a leap backwards or forwards relative to the one before it. Told-order bullet 1 is a flash-forward into the film's final act, and told-order bullets 2-4 drop back to before the accident that starts everything.
fabula_notes: The collision itself is shown only in fragments and from a distance, never as a single continuous scene. The transplant operation and Jack's time in prison are implied by their consequences rather than staged, and Cristina's pregnancy at the close is carried by Paul's closing narration rather than dramatised.
